findings.title: isDueToday() uses three local-timezone Date methods to derive a calendar date
findings.detail: Function isDueToday() at invoiceChecker.js:29-39 constructs a YYYY-MM-DD string from a Date object using d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), and d.getDate(). All three methods return values in the *local system timezone*, not UTC. The constructed string is then compared with the targetDate parameter.
findings.impactDetail: Root cause: local-TZ extraction applied to UTC input

findings.title: Input is a UTC ISO 8601 string; output assumption is implicitly local-calendar
findings.detail: The @param JSDoc declares isoTimestamp as 'ISO 8601 UTC string' (invoiceChecker.js:25). The parameter contract acknowledges the input is UTC. However, the implementation extracts the date using local-timezone methods rather than UTC methods. There is a mismatch between the declared contract (UTC input) and the implementation (local output).
findings.impactDetail: UTC input contract violated by local-TZ implementation

findings.title: The fix is documented in the source but deliberately not applied
findings.detail: The source code comment at invoiceChecker.js:16-18 explicitly documents the correct fix: 'use getUTCFullYear(), getUTCMonth(), getUTCDate()'. This confirms the bug is intentional for the SHADOWBOX demonstration. No UTC methods are present in the actual implementation body.

evidence.code: The correct fix (NOT applied here) would be to use getUTCFullYear(), getUTCMonth(), getUTCDate()

findings.impactDetail: Confirms intentional demo bug; fix path is documented

findings.title: getInvoicesDueOn() inherits the same sensitivity via isDueToday()
findings.detail: getInvoicesDueOn() at invoiceChecker.js:48-50 delegates entirely to isDueToday() per invoice. It has no independent date logic. Any failure in isDueToday() propagates to the filter result and downstream amount calculations.

findings.title: 3 of 5 tests are TZ-sensitive; 2 of 5 are TZ-independent
findings.detail: Classification of all 5 tests: TZ-SENSITIVE (fail in UTC, pass in IST): (1) 'returns true for an invoice whose UTC time crosses midnight into the target date in local TZ' - uses 2024-01-14T23:30:00Z which is Jan 15 IST but Jan 14 UTC; (2) 'returns both invoices due on 2024-01-15' - includes INV-001 which uses the same edge timestamp; (3) 'returns correct total amount for due invoices' - total depends on INV-001 inclusion (500 missing in UTC => 750 not 1250). TZ-INDEPENDENT (pass in both environments): (4) 'returns false for an invoice due on a completely different date' - uses 2024-01-01T12:00Z against Jan 15, universally false; (5) 'returns true for a clearly same-day invoice' - uses 2024-01-15T12:00Z (noon UTC), universally Jan 15 in all timezones UTC-11 to UTC+14.
findings.impactDetail: Explains exact 2-pass/3-fail split observed in reproduction

findings.title: Test failure messages embed diagnostic runtime information
findings.detail: The three failing tests include runtime diagnostics in their assertion messages: 'Current TZ: UTC', 'Resolved local date: 2024-01-14', 'INV-001 local date: 2024-01-14'. These messages are emitted by code inside the test assertion itself, not by the application. They confirm the exact mechanism at runtime.

evidence.code: Current TZ: ${process.env.TZ || '(not set)'} | Resolved local date: ${d.getFullYear()}-...

findings.impactDetail: Provides runtime confirmation of TZ mechanism in test output

findings.title: The bug only triggers for timestamps within UTC+5:30 hours of midnight
findings.detail: The local-vs-UTC calendar date can only differ when the UTC timestamp falls in the 23:00-23:59 range for a timezone ahead of UTC, or in 00:00-05:29 for IST specifically. Timestamps at noon UTC (12:00Z) are safe in any timezone that is less than 12 hours from UTC. The test intentionally chooses 23:30 UTC to be squarely in the danger zone for IST (resulting in 05:00 IST the next day).

evidence.content: IST utcOffset = +330 minutes (5h30m); edge window = 18:30-23:59 UTC

findings.impactDetail: Defines the blast radius of the bug
